items.title: Courting Controversy: Crackers and Crackdowns - Delhi’s Annual Smog Ritual
items.summary: Every Delhi resident knows the calendar. Sometime post October, the city rediscovers its need for air purifiers, school groups debate closures, the AQI app becomes the most-checked screen in the house, prime-time panels convene and the courts take up the matter of air pollution with urgency. For three or four months, it is all that anyone talks about. Then March arrives with bluer skies, the masks go back into the drawers and the city forgets, until the next October, when the conversation begins again as though for the first time. In keeping with Delhi’s cyclical conversation about its air, this column too, returns to the subject of pollution. Last year, in Crazy Little Thing Called Air , it was observed that an intermittently imposed Graded Response Action Plan (“ GRAP ”) alone was not sufficient to tackle the problem of poor air quality. A year on, the script has barely changed. This year, the air turned well before the festivities did. Delhi recorded its first poor air quality day of the season on 21 October 2026 .
